name: Store speed fix, from field data to a checked release
goal: Your store's slowest page types made faster for real visitors: a baseline from Chrome's real-visitor data, the causes found, the fixes you picked built on an unpublished theme copy, proven before and after, published on your yes, and re-checked with real-visitor data 28 days later.
starts_from: A monthly speed review, a site results readout that flagged speed, a new app or theme update that slowed the store, or you asking why the store feels slow.
metrics: Main number from context/goals.json first. For a speed job, the target is the share of phone visits that pass all three Core Web Vitals.
Real-visitor speed at the 75th percentile on phones, by page type: LCP 2.5 seconds or less, INP 200 milliseconds or less, CLS 0.1 or less.
Guardrail: conversion rate and add-to-cart rate for the changed page types do not fall after release.

stages.name: Gather what we know
stages.say: Collects the facts before any test runs: which page types earn the most (home, top collections, top products, landing pages), what changed recently (apps installed or removed, theme updates, new tracking tags), the current app list, the theme and version, and which tools we can reach. Shopify's own Web performance dashboard has no API, so it asks you for screenshots of it. Gaps become questions for you.
needs: Shopify connector or CLI (read): theme, app list, top pages by sales
screenshots of the Web performance dashboard in your Shopify admin
the task that started this job
stages.done_when: intake.md lists the pages to test with their sales share, recent changes with dates, the app list, the theme and version, the access we have, and the questions you answered.

stages.name: Real-visitor baseline
stages.say: Reads Chrome's real-visitor data (CrUX) for the store and for each chosen page, on phones and desktops, plus up to 40 weeks of weekly history to see when things changed. Field data is a 28-day window and runs about 2 days behind, so it records the exact window. Pages with too few visits for page-level data are read at store level and marked so.
needs: CrUX API and CrUX History API, with the key in the host's secret store
stages.done_when: field.md gives p75 LCP, INP and CLS by page and device with the collection window, marks which are page-level and which store-level, and shows the weekly trend with dates of known changes.

stages.name: Lab tests, middle of several runs
stages.say: Runs Lighthouse on each chosen page for phones 3 to 5 times with the same settings and keeps the middle result, because single runs jump around. It saves the raw reports so the after test can be run the same way. Lab tests find causes; they do not replace real-visitor data.
needs: local Lighthouse or Lighthouse CI, or the PageSpeed Insights API
stages.done_when: lab.md gives the median LCP, CLS and total blocking time per page with the run count, device setting and date, and names where the raw reports are saved.

stages.name: Causes and fix list
stages.say: Finds what makes each slow page slow: a lazy-loaded main image, images without sizes, render-blocking app scripts, heavy fonts, leftover code from removed apps, layout shifts from late banners. Ranks fixes by sales at risk on that page type divided by the work, and writes each as a change request for an unpublished theme copy, with its risk and undo. Any app removal is listed on its own, because removing an app can delete its data and lose a feature.
stages.signoff: You pick which fixes to make this time, and decide on any app removal knowing what feature is lost. Reply yes with the code to approve the list as written, or say which to drop. Each app removal needs its own yes later, one at a time.
stages.done_when: fix-list.md ranks each fix with its cause, page types, expected gain, effort, risk and undo, and change-requests.md has one request per fix.

stages.name: Build the fixes on an unpublished copy
stages.say: Shows you a build plan, then on your yes makes the approved fixes on an unpublished copy of your live theme, keeping a copy of every original file. Nothing shoppers see changes. It runs Theme Check on the result.
needs: an unpublished copy of the live theme
Shopify connector at level 2, or the Shopify CLI in Claude Code
stages.publish: Nothing goes live. Through the Shopify connector or the Shopify CLI (shopify theme push to the named unpublished theme): the changed theme files are written to the unpublished copy only.
stages.done_when: Every step of the build plan ran once and was read back, and build-record.md lists the theme copy id and each file changed with its original saved.

stages.name: Before and after, for your sign-off
stages.say: Runs the same lab test, same pages, same settings, same run count, on the theme copy's preview and on the live theme, and puts the medians side by side. Renders each changed page at phone and desktop sizes from saved copies, so a fix that broke the look is caught. Then writes the release plan it will show you: which files go live and how, and how to undo.
needs: preview link of the theme copy
stages.signoff: You see the before and after table, the page pictures and the release plan. Reply yes with the code to send it to publish, or say what to change.
stages.done_when: before-after.md shows the median of the same number of runs for each page before and after, every fix is shown to help or is dropped, and the renders show no visual change except the planned ones.

stages.name: Publish the fixes
stages.say: Shows you the publish plan and runs it on your yes. The safer way pushes only the changed files to the live theme, so content edits made on the live theme since the copy was taken are kept. The other way publishes the whole copy after a backup copy of the live theme exists. If you use only the Shopify connector, which cannot write to or publish the live theme, you publish from the theme library and the agent checks it. Undo: push the saved originals back, or republish the backup theme.
needs: Shopify CLI in Claude Code, or you for the publish step
stages.publish: Through the Shopify CLI: shopify theme push to the live theme id with --only for each changed file and --nodelete, which needs --allow-live; or shopify theme publish for the fixed copy after a backup copy exists. Shoppers get the faster pages from this step.
stages.done_when: Every step of the publish plan ran once and was read back, and publish-record.md lists the live theme id, the files changed, the backup theme id and the time.

stages.name: Check the live store
stages.say: Straight after publishing, runs the lab test on the live pages the same way as before, opens each on a phone-sized render, and checks a shopper can still add to cart and reach checkout. If anything broke, it stops and shows you the undo plan.
stages.done_when: live-check.md gives live lab medians next to the preview results, the cart and checkout test result, and an undo plan for anything that failed.

stages.name: Real-visitor re-check after 28 days
stages.say: Once a full 28-day window has passed since release, plus about 2 days for the data to arrive, reads CrUX again for the same pages and devices and compares with the baseline. Also reads conversion rate and add-to-cart rate for the changed page types from GA4 as a guardrail. Adds a dated lesson to context/learnings.md on which fixes paid off.
stages.done_when: field-28.md gives p75 LCP, INP and CLS before and after by page and device with both windows, the guardrail read, and the lesson appended to context/learnings.md.

intake-complete.passes_when: every heading in intake.md is filled from a named source, recent changes have dates, and missing facts are listed as answered questions, not guesses

field-numbers.passes_when: every figure in field.md matches its saved CrUX response in numbers.json

field-review.passes_when: each number names its window, device and level (page or store), thresholds are read at the 75th percentile, and field and lab data are never mixed

lab-numbers.passes_when: every median in lab.md is the middle of its saved runs

diagnosis-review.passes_when: each cause is shown in the lab report or the theme code, each fix can be built on a theme copy as written, and app removals are listed apart with what is lost

theme-check.passes_when: Theme Check reports no new errors on the changed files

code-review.passes_when: only the approved fixes were made, originals are saved, nothing was removed that a section or app still needs, and no new script was added

before-after-numbers.passes_when: every before and after median and difference recomputes from the saved runs

render.passes_when: each changed page renders at phone and desktop sizes with no HORIZONTAL OVERFLOW

visual-review.passes_when: the changed pages look the same as the live pages except for planned changes, and nothing shifts as the page loads

live-verify.passes_when: the live pages match the preview, add to cart and the path to checkout work on phone and desktop, and only the planned files changed

recheck-numbers.passes_when: every before and after figure recomputes from its saved CrUX and GA4 inputs

recheck-review.passes_when: the after window starts after the release date, both windows are 28 days, and the lesson credits only fixes the data supports
